cases.sentence: «Какая удивительная, милая и жалкая женщина», – думал он, выходя со Степаном Аркадьичем на ___.
cases.explain: «морозный воздух» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “What a marvelous, sweet and unhappy woman!” he was thinking, as he stepped out into the frosty air with Stepan Arkadyevitch.

cases.explain: «необыкновенная женщина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes,” said Levin dreamily, “an extraordinary woman! It’s not her cleverness, but she has such wonderful depth of feeling. I’m awfully sorry for her!”

cases.explain: «Другое письмо» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: At home Kouzma told Levin that Katerina Alexandrovna was quite well, and that her sisters had not long been gone, and he handed him two letters. Levin read them at once in the hall, that he might not overlook them later. One was from Sokolov, his bailiff. Sokolov wrote that the corn could not be sold, that it was fetching only five and a half roubles, and that more than that could not be got for it. The other letter was from his sister. She scolded him for her business being still unsettled.

cases.sentence: «Ну, продадим за пять с полтиной, коли не дают больше», – тотчас же с необыкновенною легкостью решил Левин ___, прежде казавшийся ему столь трудным.
cases.explain: «первый вопрос» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Well, we must sell it at five and a half if we can’t get more,” Levin decided the first question, which had always before seemed such a weighty one, with extraordinary facility on the spot. “It’s extraordinary how all one’s time is taken up here,” he thought, considering the second letter. He felt himself to blame for not having got done what his sister had asked him to do for her. “Today, again, I’ve not been to the court, but today I’ve certainly not had time.” And resolving that he would not fail to do it next day, he went up to his wife. As he went in, Levin rapidly ran through mentally the day he had spent. All the events of the day were conversations, conversations he had heard and taken part in. All the conversations were upon subjects which, if he had been alone at home, he would never have taken up, but here they were very interesting. And all these conversations were right enough, only in two places there was something not quite right. One was what he had said about the carp, the other was something not “quite the thing” in the tender sympathy he was feeling for Anna.

cases.sentence: «Удивительно, как здесь все время занято», – подумал он о ___.

cases.sentence: – Она очень милая, очень, очень жалкая, ___, – говорил он, рассказывая про Анну, ее занятия и про то, что она велела сказать.
cases.explain: «хорошая женщина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “She is a very sweet, very, very unhappy, good woman,” he said, telling her about Anna, her occupations, and what she had told him to say to her.

cases.sentence: Он сказал ей и, поверив ее ___, пошел раздеваться.
cases.explain: «спокойному тону» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: He told her, and believing in her calm tone, he went to change his coat.

cases.sentence: Наконец он успокоил ее, только признавшись, что чувство жалости в соединении с вином сбили его и он поддался ___ Анны и что он будет избегать ее.
cases.explain: «хитрому влиянию» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: It was a long while before Levin could soothe his wife. At last he succeeded in calming her, only by confessing that a feeling of pity, in conjunction with the wine he had drunk, had been too much for him, that he had succumbed to Anna’s artful influence, and that he would avoid her. One thing he did with more sincerity confess to was that living so long in Moscow, a life of nothing but conversation, eating and drinking, he was degenerating. They talked till three o’clock in the morning. Only at three o’clock were they sufficiently reconciled to be able to go to sleep.
